earlier_scan.source_named: Killian, Don 2009. Khoemana and the Griqua (phonological description; old helsinki.fi URL 404). Mossmer 2021 UCT thesis READ in full: discusses tone only, no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: du Plessis, Menán. 2018. Kora: A lost Khoisan language of the early Cape and the Gariep. Pretoria: Unisa Press / South African History Online. 429 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8407.D8 2018); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8407 .D8 2018
sources.note: Describes KORA (!Ora, kora1292), not Xiri. Ch.3 'The sounds of Kora' has 3.4 tone melodies (pp.97-102) but no stress/accent section and no stress-placement rule; p.98 notes Lloyd's acute accent 'was usually intended to indicate stress'. pp.29-30: for Giri (Xiri) only Beach 1938:326 (one paragraph of phonetic observations) and Meinhof 1930:145-152 (short vocabulary) exist.

sources.citation: Mössmer, Martin. 2021. Xri: A study of contact, and phonetic and phonological change. MA thesis, University of Cape Town. hdl 11427/35955.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Ch.5 treats segmental change (clicks, aspiration, affricates, vowels); 5.4.4 'A note on tone' p.127: only three informants produced lexical tone with regularity; 'no study has examined the tonology of Xri'. Sec.2.4 (pp.29-38) lists the only primary Xri sources: Meinhof 1930 (short wordlist), Beach 1938 (some phonological notes), Killian 2009, Haacke & Snyman 2019.

sources.citation: Killian, Don. 2009. Khoemana and the Griqua: Identity at the heart of phonological attrition. MA thesis, University of Helsinki. 112 pp. (archived copy (Internet Archive, 9 Aug 2017) of helsinki.fi/~killian/thesis/Khoemana and the)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: No word-stress statement. Ch.4 phonological sketch (pp.24-34: vowels, clicks, 4.1.3 Tones = Beach's four Korana tonemes, root classes, syllabification) has no stress/accent section. Only p.22-23 (on Lucy Lloyd's 1879 Korana notes): 'Lloyd also believed there to be a complicated stress system in Khoemana words, indicating stress with acute accent marks.' p.56: 'While phonemic tone does exist in the language, I did not have the chance to analyze it properly.' Killian lumps Griqua (Xiri) and Korana (!Ora) as one language 'Khoemana'.

sources.citation: Haacke, Wilfrid H. G. & Jan W. Snyman. 2019. Lexical proximity of a Xri corpus to Khoekhoegowab. Studies in African Linguistics 48(2): 267-328.
sources.note: Silent on word stress. Abstract and p.269: 'absence of tonal data for Xri'; assumes Xri had a pre-tonogenetic three-tone system like !Ora; 'The best information we have on Xri tone is that Beach (1938: 237) found in 1936 that "Griet Booise, a Griqua informant from Beaufort West, employed exactly the same sort of intonation" as two competent speakers of !Ora'. Segmental correspondences only.

sources.citation: Maingard, L. F. 1932. Studies in Korana history, customs and language. Bantu Studies 6(2): 103-162 (archive.org bantustudiesjour00lfma).
sources.note: KORA (Bloemhof/Links Korana), not Xiri. Sec. VI Language (c) Tones, p.150: three tones, semantic tone contrasts, 'sentence-tone, which exists very prominently in Korana'. No word-stress rule; only an incidental remark pp.158-159 that in one chief's name 'the tone and stress are on the last syllable'.

sources.citation: Meinhof, Carl. 1930. Der Koranadialekt des Hottentottischen (Beiheft 12 zur Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen). Berlin: Reimer. 152 pp. — Lautlehre incl. 'Ton' remarks; Griqua section pp.145-152.
sources.note: Only pre-war primary record of Griqua (Xiri) speech with commentary (pp.145-152) plus a Korana phonology that reportedly mentions three tones and contextual tone/accent changes; public domain and full view, but Google Books and HathiTrust both blocked our network during this compilation.

sources.citation: Haacke, Wilfrid H. G. 2013. Phonetics and phonology: Khoekhoe (incl. !Ora). In Rainer Vossen (ed.), The Khoesan Languages, 58-108 (relevant subsections). London: Routledge.
